narrative: OMX30 enters Wednesday on strong overnight momentum with global equity risk sentiment decisively positive (weighted correlation +1.130%), led by NASDAQ's +2.59% surge. The index remains in robust bull structure—10.5% above its 200-day MA and 5.0% above the 50-MA—with ADX at 79.9 confirming strong trending bias. However, RSI at 84.71 and Stochastic K/D both in extreme overbought territory (91.5/93.9) flag acute mean-reversion risk; the index now sits exactly at 52-week highs with zero room to the upside on the range. US 10Y yields fell 126bp overnight, which removes DCF compression pressure on tech but narrows NIM expansion for banks. Commodity strength (gold +3.30%, copper +0.57%) provides direct support to Boliden but oil's +1.06% rise may pressure industrial input costs. Key watch: whether overbought technicals trigger a consolidation or profit-taking ahead of US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET.
morningBrief: OMX30 likely opens 0.6–1.0% higher on Asia-US equity momentum overnight, but expect caution due to extreme technical overbought readings (RSI 84.71, Stoch 91.5). Watch for consolidation or pullback to 50-MA support (~3150) rather than fresh breakout attempts—the index is locked at 52-week highs with no room to run. Industrials (Atlas Copco, Volvo) should see modest tailwind from positive DAX/CAC opens (+0.41%/+0.14%) despite USD/SEK weakness; banks benefit from lower yields but profit-taking risk is real after sustained rally. Pharma (AstraZeneca, Essity) outperform on lower rates and defensive rotation flows. Key catalyst: US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET—soft data could extend the equity rally, but any surprise tightness risks a sharp reversal from overbought technicals. Trade accordingly; set tight stops above resistance at 3180 and watch for exhaustion signals in the first 30 minutes.
